raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my 3.8 mu.

Chili is my main crop — that's where the money is. I'll put about 2.8 mu into chili like I've been doing, and keep 1 mu for summer maize. The maize isn't really for selling, it's mostly for our family and to feed the chickens, and it gives the soil a break from chili.

For the chili, I'll start buying seedlings from the market in our town in late April. I used to try raising my own seedlings but it's too much trouble — my neighbor sister buys them and I just do the same now, about 200 yuan per mu for seedlings. I'll lay down black mulch film before transplanting — keeps the weeds down and saves water, I learned that from the extension training a couple years back.

Fertilizer for chili is where I spend the most money. Chili is hungry, especially for potassium — the old folks say "chili eats potash." Before transplanting I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base. Then after the plants set up, I topdress urea two or three times, maybe 10 kg each time, following the irrigation. Last year my chili looked a bit pale in July so I added an extra topdress — this year I'll do the same to be safe. All together maybe 25 kg N, 8 kg P, 15 kg K per mu.

Irrigation I'll do maybe 7-8 times through the season. Chili doesn't like dry spells, but the well electricity costs add up, so I water when the ground really needs it, not on a schedule. My husband does the pumping on weekends when he's back from his job in town.

Pests are the big worry with chili — aphids and thrips come early, and if we get a wet spell anthracnose can ruin a picking. I keep a sprayer ready and walk the rows twice a week. I'll use whatever the agri-shop recommends; usually I spend 100 yuan per mu on sprays through the season. I also spray herbicide once before the film goes down.

Picking chili is the killer. From July through October I pick every week or so. My mother-in-law helps, and my daughter helps on weekends when she's not at school. For two of the busiest pickings I'll hire a neighbor woman for a few days — maybe 500 yuan total.

Last year I got about 2000 kg of fresh chili per mu and sold most of it fresh to a trader who comes around. Prices were okay, not great. If I get the same this year I'll be happy. I'm not changing much — chili is risky enough without experimenting.

For the 1 mu of summer maize, I keep it simple. Plant mid-June with seed I buy at the shop — Zhengdan or whatever's on sale, about 30 yuan. One base fertilizer application of compound, one topdress of urea at the big-trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg N total. One herbicide spray after planting. I'll irrigate once or twice if it's dry. Family labor only. Expect around 450 kg/mu — enough for our household and the animals.

Total I figure I'll spend around 2,700 yuan on inputs this year, most of it on the chili. That's a lot for us but chili pays back if the weather and prices cooperate.
